result.title: Pixel is All You Need
result.comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables, including references and appendices
result.summary: Text, images, audio, touch, and even robot actions can, in principle, all be rendered onto a single canvas, suggesting an ambitious goal of unifying all modalities within vision. Language provides the natural first test. To subsume it, a visual model must reason directly over text in pixels. Across a wide range of image, video, and unified multimodal generators, however, we find that their visual generation modules cannot perform symbolic reasoning over text on the canvas. They succeed only when an underlying text module or prompt rewriter already supplies the answer, effectively reducing the generator to a mere renderer, a limitation that post-training does little to resolve. To test whether this failure stems from pixels themselves or from current training paradigms, we train a family of purely pixel-space generative models from scratch without any text pathway. With images as their sole input and output, these models read questions, write intermediate steps, and produce answers directly on the canvas. Remarkably, they exhibit hallmark behaviors of large language models. Performance improves predictably with scale following a power law. Writing intermediate steps frame by frame substantially outperforms single-frame answering, echoing chain-of-thought, while reinforcement-learning post-training further strengthens reasoning. Moreover, sharing one canvas allows the same model to reason across modalities, a capability that text-only language models lack. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of these phenomena in purely pixel-space generative models free of text tokens.

AI.brief_summary: 论文系统检验图像、视频及统一多模态生成器能否仅凭像素中的文本进行符号推理，并从零训练纯像素空间生成模型，让其在画布上读题、写出中间步骤并作答。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接考察视觉生成模型是否真正使用画布内容推理，而非依赖文本旁路；逐帧中间步骤与 RL 后训练也关联 LVR 的推理状态生成、监督和动态计算，可供对照像素空间与 latent 空间的推理路径。
